findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

I found no release-blocking defect. verify.md and ticket.md don't claim the merged head is approved: both mark beac76fc3 as historical, say merge readiness is blocked until full CI passes on the final head, and keep PR #6041 as Draft. They state that the Draft-to-Ready promotion, the ticket closure and the merge to main have not happened. The data in remote-result.json matches the quoted claims: only the v2.13.2 Go lane ran the installed-hook step (it was skipped on v2.0.0), and only the Node 24 lane ran acceptance (it was skipped on Node 22). The checks I could confirm also match the context files. The independent review 7991f5c9 approved with no errors and raised the same warnings this ticket answers. The internal `hook go-lint` action prints the result of `goLint` as JSON on stdout. The findings below are non-blocking: stale wording, a gate that was skipped but disclosed, and two answers to review warnings that the bounded context can't fully confirm.

verify.md answers the reviewer's stdout-protocol warning by saying 'update notices belong to public command setup, and bundled helpers use the pinned executable.' The supplied program.ts shows only that the `hook go-lint` action calls `console.log(JSON.stringify(...))`. It doesn't show `registerPublicCommandCatalog`, preAction hooks, or how the hook resolves the CLI (for example, whether a package-runner wrapper can print to stdout first). The claim is plausible but not proven by the files in this packet. The tests always set `SAFEWORD_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`, so they can't catch a regression here. If stdout gets polluted, every Go edit in production gets an 'invalid result' warning and is never linted. A test that runs the real hook without that variable, or a sentinel or last-line parse, would make the claim checkable.

verify.md calls `run.issues-exit-code: 0` an 'explicit customer policy' and leaves it alone. In go-lint.ts, `diagnostics()` returns early when `result.code === 0`, so findings printed to stdout are thrown away and the hook reports a clean result. This isn't a regression: the old hook behaved the same. The customer's exit-code setting governs the linter's own exit code, but it doesn't mean they want findings hidden from the editor. The disclosure is honest, but you should think about treating non-empty stdout as findings.

Full branch-wide phase-stamp review was skipped because upstream ARCHITECTURE.md exceeds the coordinator's 262144-byte limit. The scoped review 7991f5c9 covered the source targets, not the merge resolution at 83f099c6c, where conflicting plugin metadata was regenerated. The skip is disclosed and a follow-up is recorded, but the merge-resolution diff has no independent review. Only generated-surface freshness and the pending final-head CI cover it.

The historical section says 'Remote CI run 39695922147 is the current-source verification' and 'Final source/test revision: beac76fc3'. That contradicts the section's own preface, which says beac76fc3 isn't the exact head. Replacing 'current-source' with 'historical' would remove a misleading phrase someone could quote out of context.

In ticket.md's frontmatter, `last_modified` still equals `created` (2026-10-21T16:51:50.189Z), even though the work log has many later entries, including the admin-merge preparation. If tooling reads `last_modified` for freshness, it will misreport.

go-lint.ts adds raw `checked.stderr` to `warnings` with no size cap. Combined with the known plain-warning limit for Claude and Cursor, a large loader error can reach the host at full size. This is documented as an existing limit and isn't new in this change.
